authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: Don't drift into generic artifact combo that ignores sacrifice-cost abilities.
Don't build to the outdated once-per-turn/nontoken reading of Ashnod.

blueprint_failure_modes.description: Vandalblast-style wipes or Stony Silence-type locks shut off the engine.
Bolas's Citadel and Time Sieve need a big board to fire.

value.interaction: Light: Mana Drain, Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat, a few removal spells; artifact hate must be answered on the stack.
value.mana: Artifact fast mana (Mox Opal, Lotus Petal, Sol Ring, Urza's Saga) and 33 lands (lean; the dossier accepts the risk).
value.protection: Free counters; Ashnod is five mana so recasting hurts.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Ashnod doubles every non-mana ability that sacrificed something to activate: copied Time Sieve is two extra turns, copied Trading Post is two cards or two artifacts back.
accepted_role.honest_note: The source blueprint describes an older 'once each turn, nontoken' Ashnod; current Oracle has no turn limit and tokens count (M1 ashnod-01). The deck is stronger than the source text implies, and its infinites run without Ashnod.
